rows.what: The opening run follows the Design Release 2.1 step order: import reason before commodity details, no CPH step in the run, a skip to the overview when everything is already complete, and the run always ends on the review page, which names anything outstanding. Also rewrites the tests repo's cattle-by-air walk.
rows.plantsWork: Only the run ending changes in plants. After the last step (consignment-contact-select), the run goes to the review page (notification-view) instead of the overview, even when the notification is incomplete, and the review names what is outstanding. Plants keeps its own step order. The step reorder, the CPH removal and the cattle walk are animals only.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main has the same opening-run mechanism (RUN_STEPS/nextRunTarget in sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/flow/run.js), but it always falls through to hubPath after consignment-contact-select and has no review step. Animals already has a reviewTarget step. Most of the row is the animals step order (import reason, CPH, identification), which plants does not share.

rows.what: A page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on 'Save and continue' instead of running on to the next page in its section. The address stays the same and no from=hub marker is added. The opening run from the dashboard still chains page to page.
rows.plantsWork: Change the fallback in plants' kit.nextTarget (outside the opening run) from moving to the next page in the section to returning to the overview, so a hub-opened page such as consignor-select no longer runs on into identification-numbers. Plants' multi-page task rows (commodities: type to list; arrival: status to details) must still move within their own row.
rows.why: Plants' shared/kit.js nextTarget has the same fallback as animals: exitTarget(runTarget ?? nextInSection). Its 'parties' section in flow/flow.js puts two separate overview rows (consignor, identificationNumbers) in one section, so a hub-opened consignor page chains to identification numbers. Animals' Roles and addresses to CPH chain is the same pattern.

rows.what: 'Save and return to overview' saves what was entered without the page's required-answer checks and goes to the overview. The task does not read Complete, but format errors are still refused. A named few pages keep their required checks.
rows.plantsWork: Plants' question pages that carry exit=hub (origin, commodity-type, arrival-status, arrival-details, place-of-destination, consignor, identification numbers) skip the required-answer check when 'Save and return to overview' is pressed, but still refuse malformed answers. The same exit=hub branch is used. This overlaps EUDPA-667's mandatory-to-proceed versus mandatory-to-submit work, which already makes plants default to mandatory to submit.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main has the same exit=hub button (shared/save-actions.njk) and hubExitTarget in shared/kit.js. Its controllers, for example features/origin/controller.js, validate required answers before checking exit=hub, so a blank 'Save and return to overview' is refused today, as in animals.

rows.what: While amending, pages end with 'Save and return' (to the amend review), 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview', with no cancel link. Party pickers have two buttons only. Back links stay unchanged. Continue on the amend review is silently held while anything is incomplete or invalid.
rows.plantsWork: Give plants' save-actions partial the same three amend-mode controls, using exit=hub and ?change=1 with no new field, and the same two-button ending on its party pickers (consignor, place of destination, contact). Plants' check-answers POST in AMEND stays on the review with no error summary when incomplete. Today it redirects to the hub or shows errors.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main supports amendment (AMEND status, features/cancel-amend, the amend action on the dashboard, cancelAmendHref on check-answers). It uses an identical shared/save-actions.njk with no amend mode, and its check-answers POST shows errors or redirects to the hub when the notification is incomplete.

rows.what: A tests-only end-to-end walk of a horse-by-sea notification under temporary admission, from create to submitted.
rows.why: The walk uses horse, temporary admission, microchip and passport, and the registered equine answer. These are live-animal content with no plants equivalent; the plants journey on origin/main (sets/high-risk-plants) has its own commodity types and happy path.

themes.summary: Plants runs on the same journey engine as animals: the same kit.nextTarget fallback, opening-run RUN_STEPS, exit=hub save-actions partial, amend status and check-answers review. So the run ending on the review page, the return to the overview, lenient 'Save and return to overview' and the amend-mode page endings all apply to both frontends in the same increments. Plants keeps its own step order, so the animals step reorder, the CPH removal and both animal end-to-end walks (cattle, horse) do not apply to it. Lenient 'Save and return to overview' overlaps the EUDPA-667 mandatory-to-submit work.

rows.what: The transhipment and transit 'Destination country' selects offer the same countries and subdivisions as the country of origin page, labelled '<territory> (<parent>)', in one A to Z list, with existing saved answers still shown selected.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main has no import-reason page, no transhipment or transit reason and no destination-country select. A grep of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants for transhipment, transit, destinationCountry and port of exit finds only spec JSON and unrelated test text. The change sits in the animals import-reason feature folder only.

rows.what: Reference data returns each port's type from MDM's traffic field, and the port of entry list is ordered airports, then seaports, then rail. Each group is A to Z ignoring letter case and treating odd spaces as single spaces. Both port of exit selects take the same order and the same label as the port of entry options.
rows.plantsWork: Plants' port of landing autocomplete on arrival details lists reference data's /ports-of-entry in the order it arrives (services/ports/index.js portOptions), so in real mode the new order arrives without a code change. The captured ports fixture is byte-identical to animals' and needs recapturing in the new order in the same increment. If the shared port label changes from 'name (code)' to 'name - code', plants' displayName in services/ports/index.js changes the same way. Plants has no port of exit, so that half is animals-only.
rows.why: Plants has the same ports service: src/server/app/services/ports/client.js fetches /ports-of-entry, and arrival-details/controller.js offers ports.portOptions(). Its fixture src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json is the same blob as animals' (b71bea2). The criteria say the port of entry label is '<name> - <code>', but both frontends label ports '<name> (<code>)' on origin/main. The build should settle which label is meant before matching plants.

rows.what: The stub tidy-up. The stub serves MDM's real countries (250, or 32 for GBNAG_SPS_EX) and real ports, each record whole. Every frontend's captured country and port fixtures are recaptured from it, stub-mode lists match what reference data serves, and the end-to-end specs take names and counts from the recaptured fixture.
rows.plantsWork: Rerun plants' capture script against the tidied stub and commit the regenerated countries.json, countries-origin.json and ports-of-entry.json, so plants' stub mode offers the same lists as reference data. Then fix any plants unit, fit or tests-repo plants specs that pin the old names or counts. Plants' capture.js already treats every target as a built endpoint, so the 'waiting on an endpoint' change is animals-only.
rows.why: Plants has the same _capture layer on origin/main (src/server/app/services/_capture/capture.js, fixtures/*.json), feeding the stub-mode countries and ports services. Its countries.json and ports-of-entry.json are byte-identical to animals' (bff57be, b71bea2), so they go stale in the same way. Its countries-origin.json is a copy of the unfiltered 31-country list, which a recapture would also correct. The 'not built' marking exists only in the animals capture.js (optional: true on ports-of-entry).

themes.summary: Plants shares the reference-data layer: its countries and ports services and captured fixtures are the same as the animals frontend's, and its arrival-details port of landing autocomplete reads the same /ports-of-entry list. So the stub tidy-up's fixture recapture and the port of entry order also land in plants in the same increments. Plants has no import-reason page, no transhipment or transit destination country and no port of exit, so the destination-country row and the port of exit half of the port row stay animals-only. One open point: the port row says port of entry options read 'name - code', but both frontends show 'name (code)' today, so which label is meant needs settling before plants is matched.

rows.what: Country of origin becomes a search box: no hint, a 'Search for a country' placeholder, no list on focus, a search icon in place of the drop-down arrow, matching on letters anywhere in the name with the matches in bold, screen-reader labels and announcements, and Welsh for all of it.
rows.plantsWork: Give the plants 'Country of origin' control the same search-box behaviour: drop the 'Start typing to search for a country.' hint, use the 'Search for a country' placeholder with JavaScript (keep the blank 'Select a country' option without it), turn off showAllValues, add the search icon and remove the arrow, use contains-matching with bold matches, and add the results label and announcements in English and Welsh. Plants keeps its own country list, its narrowing guidance and its errors; change the copy of the autocomplete component in plants the same way as in animals.
rows.why: Plants has the same origin page on origin/main. src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk uses the same appAccessibleAutocomplete macro for countryOfOrigin with showAllValues: true, and copy.en.js has the hint and the 'Select a country' placeholder this row removes or replaces.

rows.what: Finishing the origin page: the region of origin code hint, a 5-character limit, the live country prefix, clearing the code when the answer changes to No, and the completeness rule for the 'where from' task. Also the shorter internal reference hint, the Welsh pass and a new visual baseline.
rows.why: Almost all of the row is the region of origin code from the animal health certificate. The plants origin page collects countryOfOrigin and nothing else, and journey-spec.json records that region code is deliberately not copied to plants. The one shared part, the internal reference hint, is already done: plants keeps its optional reference as consignmentNumber on the identification-numbers page, and that hint ('Any reference you use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.') has no 58-character sentence.

rows.what: The country of origin list shows each subdivision with its parent country, for example 'Canary Islands (Spain)'. The list is sorted by the label shown, and searching for the parent country finds the subdivision too.
rows.why: In plants, originCountries (src/server/app/services/countries/index.js on origin/main) maps only the GBNAG_SPS_EX countries and never reads subDivisions, so the plants origin list has no subdivisions to label. Animals' subdivisions come with its region code handling (originCountryOptions, parentCountryCode). Whether plants should offer subdivisions at all, for example for the Balearic Islands exclusion on ware potatoes, is a question for the plants requirements, not part of this change.

themes.summary: Only one of the three rows needs a change in plants. The plants origin page uses the same country type-ahead, with a hint, a 'Select a country' placeholder and the full list on focus, so the country search box change (inc-009) should be made to both frontends in the same increment. The region of origin code row is animal-health content plants does not collect, and its only shared part, the internal reference hint, already matches in plants. The subdivision label row has no plants equivalent because the plants country list has no subdivisions.

Plants shares almost nothing in this theme. Its commodities are an add-another list (commodity type, then a list page, then a details sub-page per line, with category, genus by autocomplete and quantity). There is no search page, no species chips, no live-animal catalogue, no packages, no main import reason page, no additional details page and no transport. Every row is either animal content or a page and behaviour plants does not have, so no row needs to change plants. Two general patterns sit in other themes' rows, not these: whether a "Save and return to overview" with nothing entered should still validate (the shared soft-save foundation), and whether back links follow the journey order rather than going to the hub (the journey-foundation order).

rows.what: Wording on the commodity search page and Commodity details: the ITAHC inset text, the live-animals search hint, the Trade Tariff 'opens in a new tab' line, the 'Description of the goods' caption, a Species column in the Selected commodities table, error summary ordered question by question across species, and Welsh drafts.
rows.why: The changes are about ITAHCs, species, Latin names and animal and package counts for each species. On origin/main, plants' features/commodities has no search page, no inset, no 'Help with commodity codes' details and no table of species for each line. Its details page edits one line at a time, so there is no error order across lines. Its caption comes from section-captions/index.js ('About the consignment'), and plants keeps its own section names.

rows.what: The live-animal commodity catalogue: the commodities and species DR2.1 adds, Cow renamed to Cattle, germinal lines removed, which commodities ask for packages, and the k6 search term.
rows.why: This is the live-animal catalogue in the animals commodity service. Plants has its own catalogue of categories and genera in services/commodities/index.js, which this row does not touch.

rows.what: Commodity search results are sorted and show the match in bold. The selected panel shows each species as a Latin-name chip with a remove button. The 'Select a commodity' error moves. 'Save and return to overview' saves without checking. Saving clears the unweaned answer for 01061900. All of this still works without JavaScript.
rows.why: Plants has no commodity search, no results, no chips and no unweaned answer. features/commodities/list is a table of added lines with Change and Remove. One part looks related: plants' list POST refuses an empty list whichever button is pressed. Whether that stays is the shared soft-save foundation row's call, not this row's.

rows.what: The commodity search lists results as the trader types (with JavaScript), fetched from the service, with a live region, tick-to-add, Escape to close, and the no-JavaScript fallback kept.
rows.why: Plants has no commodity search component. Its only type-ahead is the accessible-autocomplete genus select on details.njk, which works from a short list already in the page. That is a different component with a different need.

rows.what: The commodity page and Commodity details become steps in the journey around the main import reason page: back links go to origin or to the commodity page, the next steps go to reason, identification, additional details and arrival, and the k6 walk changes to match.
rows.why: The order is built around animals' main import reason, identification and additional details pages, and flow.js on plants origin/main has none of them (commodity type, then commodities, then details, then origin). Plants' list page links back to the hub. Whether plants' back links should follow its own journey order is a journey-foundation decision, not part of this row.

rows.what: Two required answers that block saving: means of transport on arrival details (with the other arrival fields optional), and number of packages on the commodity lines that ask for it.
rows.why: Plants collects no transport details (journey-spec.json says no transport section exists in any plants source), and arrival.js holds date, time and landing as statutory mandatory answers. Plants commodity lines have no number of packages; quantity is already required.

rows.what: A tests-only end-to-end walk of a poultry-by-rail transit notification.
rows.why: A live-animals journey (chicken, transit, rail, transporter, CPH) that only exists in the animals tests. Plants has no transit or transport.

rows.what: Wording on the main import reason page and the additional details page: the 'Main import reason' heading and title, 'Select one' as the first option of each select with no divider, the ITAHC certification hint, review labels, and Welsh.
rows.why: Plants has no reason or additional details page (services.md and journey-spec.json say no plants source asks a reason-for-import question). Plants' own selects (origin, place of landing, genus) are type-aheads with their own placeholders and already have no divider. This row does not change them.

rows.what: Where the main import reason and additional details pages sit in the journey, with their back links and next steps.
rows.why: Neither page exists in plants. flow.js on origin/main has no reason or additional details section.

rows.what: The main import reason task completes on its own answers, and 'Save and return to overview' on the reason and additional details pages saves without the required-answer checks.
rows.why: Plants has neither page or task. The general soft-save rule belongs to the shared soft-save foundation row (inc-003), which is not part of this theme.

rows.what: The unweaned animals question is asked for pigs as well as cattle.
rows.why: Unweaned animals is animal content, and plants has no additional details page.

rows.what: Move the animals arrival details page from the port-of-entry address to an arrival-details address (dropped by the 9 October ruling).
rows.why: Dropped, so nothing to build. For the record, plants already serves its arrival details page at the 'arrival-details' slug (arrival-details/page.js on origin/main).

rows.what: Arrival details wording: question labels go up to the medium label size, new port hint ('...search by port or airport name or code'), a 'Select a port' placeholder, means of transport options relabelled Air/Rail/Road/Sea, and a new lead-in for the transport identification hint.
rows.plantsWork: Plants' arrival details labels (date, the potato time and place of landing) move from govuk-label--s to govuk-label--m to match. The place of landing hint follows the same 'Start typing to search by port or airport name or code.' pattern while keeping its own lead sentence. Plants has no means of transport or transport identification, so those parts are animals only. Its 'Select a place of landing' placeholder already follows the placeholder pattern.
rows.why: Plants has the same page on origin/main (sets/high-risk-plants/.../arrival-details/template.njk): a date picker, plus a port autocomplete for potatoes built on the same appAccessibleAutocomplete component, also using small bold labels and a 'Start typing to search by port name or code' hint. kit.dateField sets the date label size, so the date label change touches plants' shared/kit.js.

rows.what: Port and transit country searches: options read 'name - code', the chosen port shows as 'name - code', a 'Search' button sits beside the box, and the typed text shows in bold in the matches. Without JavaScript the native selects stay.
rows.plantsWork: Plants' ports service displayName changes from 'Name (CODE)' to 'Name - CODE', and plants' own copy of the accessible-autocomplete component gets the same Search button and bold match, so the potato place of landing search (and the other searches that use the component) behave as they do in animals. Plants has no transit countries page, so that part is animals only.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main has its own copy of services/ports/index.js, with the same `${name} (${code})` display, and its own accessible-autocomplete macro and client script. The place of landing search on plants' arrival-details page was copied from animals' portOfEntry (journey-spec.json widgetDetail).

rows.what: Arrival details requires a means of transport. Arrival details and transit countries return to the overview or the review depending on where the user came from. 'Save and return to overview' skips required checks but keeps the format checks.
rows.why: The means of transport error and the transit countries parts are animals only. Plants' arrival-details controller and kit.nextTarget/exitTarget on origin/main have the same Save and continue / Save and return shape: everything is validated before the exit=hub check. Two things would settle it. First, whether inc-002 (journey-foundation) builds return-to-overview into both frontends' shared kit; if it does, plants arrival details gets it from there. Second, whether 'Save and return skips required checks' is a page rule here or a platform rule owned by the mandatory-to-proceed work (EUDPA-667). If it is a page rule, plants' date-only arrival details page should follow it.

rows.what: Transit countries page: page title, a Back link that depends on where the user came from, no empty-state sentence, and a redirect to the overview when the means of transport is Air, Sea or not given.
rows.why: Plants has no transit countries page and no means of transport question. Under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants on origin/main, the only arrival features are arrival-status and arrival-details.

rows.what: With JavaScript, transit countries are added and removed in place, with 'Added' and 'Removed' screen reader announcements. The no-JavaScript fallback and the duplicate and 12-country limits stay.
rows.why: Plants has no transit countries page or other add-and-remove country list on origin/main. Its status-announcer.js exists but has no matching page to use it here.

rows.what: The transit country search offers the GBNAG_SPS_EX countries and their subdivisions, with subdivisions labelled '<territory> (<parent country>)'.
rows.why: Plants has no transit countries page on origin/main. Its country of origin list (features/origin) belongs to the origin and reference-lists themes, not this row.

themes.summary: Plants has an arrival details page of its own: a date, plus a time and a place of landing search for potatoes. It uses the same autocomplete component and a copy of the same ports service, so the label-size and hint wording row (inc-026) and the port search display row (inc-027) should change both frontends in the same increment. Plants has no means of transport question and no transit countries page, so the transit rows (inc-029, inc-030, inc-174) have no plants equivalent. The return-and-validation row (inc-028) is unsure until we know whether journey-foundation and EUDPA-667 bring that behaviour to plants. The dropped address move (inc-025) already matches: plants already uses the 'arrival-details' address.

rows.what: Let the trader open the Upload documents page from the overview as soon as the origin is answered, without first finishing the commodity or later sections.
rows.why: Plants has no documents page or documents task row. origin/main src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/ has no documents folder, and sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md says there is no document-upload service and a page that attaches a file is out of scope.

rows.what: Update the Upload documents page to match the new design: guidance table wording, the document reference and date of issue hints, the attachment size and file-type bullets, the added-documents table headings, removing the empty-state text, and showing the 15-file maximum error inline on the Attachment field.
rows.why: The page exists only in animals (sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents). Plants on origin/main has no upload page, table or attachment field (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md, 'Out of scope').

rows.what: Let document references include punctuation such as hyphens, slashes and spaces (a backend check), and reorder the document type list, removing Health certificate.
rows.why: Plants has no document entry, document type select or document-upload backend call on origin/main (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md). The type list is also animal-specific, for example ITAHC and veterinary health certificate.

rows.what: Make the Upload documents page remember where the trader opened it from (the journey, the overview, the review page or amending a notification), and send its Back link and Save and continue back there, including after adding, removing or a validation error.
rows.why: The change is to the documents page's own return handling. Plants has no documents page (no features/documents under sets/high-risk-plants on origin/main). Any shared change-context fallback is owned by the journey-foundation rows, not this one.

rows.what: Stop Save and continue waiting for virus scans, while still blocking a document that has a virus, and make Save and return to overview save a fully filled-in document or show its errors.
rows.why: Plants has no uploads, virus scanning or documents controller. sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md on origin/main rules out uploads entirely.

rows.what: Raise the attachment size limit to 50MB, with the matching guidance and errors with and without JavaScript. Blocked by a platform limit.
rows.why: Blocked. Plants has no file attachment on origin/main (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md). The only other set the row names is germinal products, not plants.

themes.summary: Plants has nothing in common with this theme. Its origin/main has no Upload documents page, no documents task on the overview, no virus scanning and no document-upload service, and its services doc lists file attachment as out of scope. All six rows change animals only, so none needs a matching change in plants.

rows.what: The private transporter's Country select offers reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus the United Kingdom, exactly as MDM serves them.
rows.why: Plants has no transporter pages or transporter service. Its services.md on origin/main says the transport and transporter services were removed because the journey collects no transport details (behaviour customs-no-sps-hold-or-matching). Plants' own country selects use a different list and are not affected.

rows.what: The transporter list is brought in line with DR2.1: a 'Select a transporter' sub-heading, an icon search button with in-page filtering and a server-side fallback, search by type and status, 'Not applicable' when there is no approval number, the DR2.1 shipped commercial and private transporters, and accessibility checks on the error and empty-search states.
rows.why: Plants on origin/main has no transporter list or transporter register: a grep under src/ finds the word only in docs, specs and a status-structure comment. The shipped records are also animal transporter data.

rows.what: The 'Choose a transporter type' page gets DR2.1 copy, refuses a blank or invalid choice, sends the add forms back to it when no type is chosen, and drops the status strip on this page and the private form.
rows.why: Plants has no transporter-type page or add-transporter forms on origin/main, so there is nothing to mirror.

rows.what: Saving an added transporter goes back to the list with that transporter chosen and a one-time success banner. Both add forms get 'Save and continue' and 'Cancel and return to dashboard', unsaved values are kept, and added transporters stay with the organisation.
rows.why: Plants has no add-a-transporter forms and no organisation transporter register. Its consignor and other parties come from the INS address-book picker, which has no inline add form (rulings.json c-026 parks a typed consignor fallback).

rows.what: 'Add a private transporter' gets the DR2.1 heading and title, loses its intro paragraph, and gets a Country select that defaults to the UK with no placeholder and alphabetical order. A blank save lists the required-field errors in order.
rows.why: There is no private transporter form in plants on origin/main. The country default and order apply only to this form's select.

rows.what: 'Add a commercial transporter' gets the DR2.1 heading and title, an 'Important' authorisation banner, 'Postcode or Zip code' copy and messages, an authorisation-number message, and blank-form validation in order.
rows.why: Plants has no commercial transporter form, and the authorisation guidance applies only to animal transporters.

rows.what: (Blocked) Adds an address search to the commercial transporter form that is limited to Northern Ireland BT postcodes. Picking a result fills the empty address fields, and with JavaScript the manual fields stay hidden until the trader reveals them.
rows.why: The row is blocked. Plants has no commercial transporter form, and on origin/main it fills addresses only from the address-book picker, never from a postcode lookup (rulings.json, consignor-typed-fallback).

rows.what: 'Save and continue' on the transporter list goes to 'Upload documents' during the journey run, or back to the overview when the trader opened the list from its task.
rows.why: Plants has no transporter list. Its services.md also says it has no document-upload service, so neither end of this step exists there.

rows.what: Removes the unlinked commercial transporter register page (/transporters/select), and commercial transporters picked from the list still save with their type.
rows.why: Plants never had a transporters-select page. Only the animals live-animals set has features/transport/transporters-select.

themes.summary: Plants has no transporter pages or behaviour. On origin/main, trade-imports-plants-frontend removed its transport and transporter services because the high-risk plants journey collects no transport details (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md). Every row in this theme changes only the animals frontend, and none needs a matching plants change in the same increment.

rows.what: Places the animal identification page in the linear journey straight after Commodity details. It covers the back link from each entry point, skipping the page when no species needs identifiers, and continuing to Additional details or Arrival details.
rows.why: The page records each animal's identifiers and appears only when a species has identifier fields. Plants has no per-commodity identification step. Its 'identification-numbers' page is about supplier and producer registration numbers and sits in the parties section of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js, so it is not the same page or flow position.

rows.what: Adds a Species column to the 'Selected commodities' summary, and groups identification as one section per commodity with one panel per species.
rows.why: This is the summary and per-species panel structure of the animal identification page (species, number of animals). Plants has no species-level identification panels; its commodities list/details pages under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/commodities/ are a separate pattern.

rows.what: Each species panel's 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' saves only that species' current animal. The saved-animals table moves below the form, the panel shows only the table once every animal is entered, and the panel button becomes primary.
rows.why: This is the per-animal record entry inside species panels. Plants has no per-animal or per-species record panels anywhere under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/.

rows.what: A species panel saved with every identifier blank is refused on that panel's own save, even when another panel is filled. One identifier is enough to save.
rows.why: This validates the per-animal identifier panel, which plants does not have. The plants identification-numbers page validates its own fixed fields with ordinary required and length rules (features/identification-numbers/controller.js).

rows.what: Dropped. Would have made identification count as complete only when every animal is entered, and required one entry per species before submitting.
rows.why: Dropped because the 9 October ruling adopted what the service does today. It was about counting animal identification entries anyway, and plants has no per-animal entries.

rows.what: Identifier labels and hints follow DR2.1: 'Microchip' instead of 'Microchip number' and no hint text. Length errors say '58 characters or less', and values are trimmed before the length check, with matching Welsh drafts.
rows.why: The labels and hints are animal identifiers (microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name). The shared wording pattern is already in plants: identification-numbers/copy/copy.en.js says 'must be 58 characters or less', and lib/validate/validators.js trims with Joi before the length check. Plants needs no change.

rows.what: Pigs, sheep and goats are identified by ear tag only, with an Animal / Ear tag / Remove saved-animals table.
rows.why: This is species-specific identifier content. Plants has no animal species or ear tags.

themes.summary: Every row in this theme builds or fills the new germinal products set in the animals frontend. That set is not on origin/main yet: the only germinal mentions there are in services and live-animals copy. The rows copy live-animals pages into the germinal set and add germinal-only questions, validation, cards and obligations, so none changes a page or behaviour that plants shares. Plants needs no change for this theme, and no row should touch trade-imports-plants-frontend.
